title.en: Seventy Thousand Who Enter Paradise Without Account
title.zh: 無算而入樂園的七萬人

region.en: Medina, teaching on the Weighing (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那關於清算的教導（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tawhid, no. 7437; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tawhid, no. 7437 — narrated by Ibn Abbas

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without account: those who do not draw omens, nor treat by cautery or incantation, but trust their Lord — and a further crowd like them. They are the ones who do not believe in ill omens, do not seek ruqya, do not cauterize, and upon their Lord alone they rely. So many gather that they are said to be like the clouds of the morning.
summary.zh: 我的教民中有七萬人將無算而入樂園：不占卜、不以烙治或咒術治病，而信賴其主——另有與他們相仿的一群。他們不以凶兆為懼、不求符咒、不施烙術，惟倚賴其主。其眾之多，如晨雲。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Prophet said: Seventy thousand, or seven hundred thousand, of my nation will enter Paradise without account; they are those who do not treat themselves with ruqya (incantations), nor believe in omens, nor are treated by cautery, and they put their trust in their Lord. Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether the Prophet said seventy thousand or seven hundred thousand. And Ukkashah was of the same description; so he said, 'O Lord, make me one of them.' The Prophet said, 'You are one of them.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tawhid, no. 7437; not verbatim.

title.en: Musa Slaps the Angel of Death

region.en: Mount Nebo region, Israelite wilderness (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 尼波山地區，以色列曠野（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fada'il (also Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1339); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih Muslim, Kitab Fada'il al-Sahabah — narrated by Abu Hurayrah (parallel: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1339)

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Angel of Death is sent to Musa; when he meets him, Musa slaps him between the eyes. The angel returns to God: 'You have sent me to a slave who does not want to die.' God restores his eye and says: 'Return to My servant and tell him — put your hand on the back of an ox: you will live for the number of hairs that fall under it.' 'My Lord, then what?' — 'Then death.' Musa asks to be brought near the Holy Land by a stone's throw, and it is said that he was buried there.
summary.zh: 死神天使奉遣至穆薩；相遇之際，穆薩一掌擊其眼間。天使歸主：『你遣我至一不欲死之僕。』主復其眼而諭：『回去告訴我的僕人——把手放在牛背上：其下落毛之數即其壽數。』『我的主，那之後呢？』——『之後便是死。』穆薩求葬於聖地一石之距，相傳其墓即在該地。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; the episode belongs to the 'origin of death' cluster (the Angel's retreat is denied — death is fixed).

passages.text: The Angel of Death was sent to Moses. When he came to Moses, Moses slapped him severely on the eye. The angel returned to his Lord and said, 'You have sent me to a slave who does not want to die.' God restored his eye and said, 'Go back and tell him to place his hand on the back of an ox and to tell you, by the number of hairs that fall under it, how long he will live.' Moses placed his hand on the back of an ox, and the hair that fell under his palm was one: and God said, 'You will live for one hair's worth, and then you will die.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab Fada'il (parallel Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1339); not verbatim.

passages.text: Moses said, 'My Lord, then what?' God said, 'Then death.' Moses said, 'Bring me near the Holy Land by a stone's throw'; and it is said that Moses was buried there, in the land nearest to the Holy Land, so that his place of burial was a stone's throw from Jerusalem.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab Fada'il (parallel Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1339); not verbatim.

title.en: The Jewish Boy at the Point of Death

region.en: Medina, sickroom of a Jewish boy (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那猶太男孩病榻（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1356; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1356 — narrated by Anas ibn Malik

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A Jewish boy served the Prophet, and when he fell ill the Prophet went to visit him, sat near his head and said to him: 'Embrace Islam.' The boy looked at his father, who was sitting beside him, and the father said: 'Obey Abu al-Qasim.' And the boy said the testimony: 'I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.' The Prophet went out saying: 'Praise be to God who saved him from the Fire.'
summary.zh: 一猶太男孩服侍先知；男孩病重，先知探視，坐於其頭旁，對他說：『你當入伊斯蘭。』男孩望向坐在旁邊的父親；父親說：『聽阿布·卡西姆的話。』男孩遂念清真言：『我作證除真主外別無神明，穆罕默德是其僕人與使者。』先知出門說：『讚美主，他因得救於火獄。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; interfaith dimension noted for comparative study.

passages.text: A young Jewish boy used to serve the Prophet and used to fetch him water for ablution. One day the boy fell ill, and the Prophet went to visit him, sat near his head, and said to him: 'Embrace Islam.' The boy looked at his father, who was sitting with him, and the father said to him, 'Obey Abu al-Qasim.' And the boy embraced Islam. The Prophet went out of the house saying: 'Praise be to God who saved him from the Fire through me.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jana'iz, no. 1356; not verbatim.

title.en: The Man Who Killed Ninety-Nine Souls

region.en: Road between two villages of the Israelites (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 以色列人兩村之間的道路（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766 (variant: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Da'awat, no. 347); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766 — narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A man kills ninety-nine people and asks about the possibility of repentance. A monk says there is no way; a worshipper of God says it is possible — 'Go to such a land, for there are people there who worship God, so worship God as they do.' He sets out; death overtakes him on the road. The angel of mercy and the angel of punishment dispute him; God sends a third angel: measure the distance to the two lands, and to whichever he is nearer, to it he belongs. And the earth is ordered to stretch on one side and draw in on the other: he is found nearer the land of obedience — and he is forgiven.
summary.zh: 一人殺了九十九人，求問可否懺悔。一僧言無路；一敬拜者言可——『往某地，那裡有人敬拜主，你便如他們敬拜主。』他啟程，途中遇死。仁慈天使與懲罰天使相爭；主遣第三位：量兩地之距，其近者屬之。大地奉命一側延伸、一側收攏：其近善地——遂蒙赦宥。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: There was among the people of the Israelites a man who had killed ninety-nine people. He asked about the most learned man of the earth, and was directed to a monk; he came to him and said, 'I have killed ninety-nine people; is there any repentance for me?' The monk said, 'No.' So he killed him, and completed one hundred. Then he asked about the most learned man of the earth, and was directed to a worshipper; and he said to him, 'I have killed a hundred men; is there any repentance for me?' He said, 'Yes; nothing can stand between you and repentance. Go to such and such a land, where there are people who worship God; worship God along with them and do not come back to your land, for it is an evil land.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766; not verbatim.

passages.text: So he set out, and when he had covered half of the way death overtook him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed about him. God commanded the earth on either side to draw near, and He commanded the earth he was nearer to draw near, and the other to draw away; then He said: Measure the distance between them. It was found he was nearer the land he was going to by a hand's breadth; so he was forgiven. It was said to Abu Sa'id: While he was in this state, the breath of death came to him, and the earth was commanded to draw him to the land of righteousness.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Tawbah, no. 2766; not verbatim.

title.en: Tamim al-Dari's Voyage: The Island of Dajjal
title.zh: 塔米姆·達里的航海：怪者之島

region.en: Open sea, island of the one-eyed man (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 大洋中獨眼人所在之島（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2937 (long hadith of al-Jassasah); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan wa Ashrat al-Sa'ah, no. 2937 — narrated by Fatima bint Qays

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Tamim al-Dari, a Christian who came to Islam, tells the Prophet of a voyage: a storm carried their ship to an island where they met a shaggy beast, al-Jassasah (the spy), who ran from them, and a huge man bound with heavy chains in a monastery, who asked them news of the spring of Zarka, of the palm-groves of Baysan, of the lake of Tiberias, of the water of the sea, of the Prophet of the Arabs who had appeared. He announces that he is Dajjal, the Antichrist: 'I shall shortly be permitted to come out, and I shall travel the earth in forty days, leaving no town untouched.' The Prophet tells the story in the mosque, and warns of the signs of the Hour.
summary.zh: 已入教的基督徒塔米姆·達里向先知講述其航行：風暴使船漂至一島，遇一毛茸之獸——『窺探者』（賈薩薩），奔走避人；又於修道院見一鎖以重鏈之巨人，詢問魯克泉、貝桑椰棗林、太巴列湖水、海水、以及阿拉伯新出現之先知的消息。他自言即『大騙子』（丹加勒）：『不久我將獲准出來，四十日內遍行大地，無一城不至。』先知在清真寺講述此事，並警示末時之兆。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; apocalyptic imagery treated as text within the tradition.

passages.text: Tamim al-Dari, a man who was a Christian and came to Islam, told the Prophet of a voyage he made: We sailed in the sea till we were carried by a great wind to an island, and we came to a shaggy beast with thick hair, from whose head we could not see his legs. We said, 'Woe to you, what are you?' It said, 'I am al-Jassasah. Go to this man in the monastery.' And when we came to him he was bound with heavy iron chains. He asked us about news of the spring of Zarka, of the date-palms of Baysan, of the lake of Tiberias, of the water of the sea, of the shepherd of the camels of the Arabs, and of the Prophet of the Arabs who has appeared.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2937; not verbatim.

passages.text: The bound man said: 'I am the Dajjal (Antichrist), and I shall shortly be permitted to come out. I shall travel the earth and shall not leave any town without entering it, except Mecca and Medina. And there will be formed for me a door of the city of Medina. And the unbelievers will be with me, and the believers will know me as a believer knows the boy in his mother's lap.' The Prophet told the story in the mosque on the pulpit, and said: 'I have kept you informed of the Dajjal, and Tamim has told me his story.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2937; not verbatim.

title.en: Ismail's Doorstep and the Kaaba Builders
title.zh: 易司馬儀的門檻與築天房者

region.en: Mecca, Ismail's dwelling (symbolic pin at the Kaaba)
region.zh: 麥加易司馬儀居所（象徵性定位於天房）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3364-3365; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3364-3365 — narrated by Ibn Abbas

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Ibrahim visits Ismail, who has married a woman of the Jurhum. 'Where is your husband?' — 'He has gone to look for food.' 'Give him my salutation and tell him to change the threshold of his gate' — meaning the wife. On a second visit, after the wife has been changed: 'Is your husband at home? Tell him to keep the threshold of his gate.' And on a third visit the two build together the House: Ibrahim stands on a stone, Ismail hands him the stones — and the stone of Ibrahim still bears the prints of his feet.
summary.zh: 易卜拉欣探視已娶主爾胡姆女子為妻的易司馬儀。『你丈夫在哪裡？』——『出外覓食。』『代我問候他，並告訴他換掉門檻』——意指其妻。換妻後再訪：『告訴他守住門檻。』第三次，父子同建天房：易卜拉欣立於一石之上，易司馬儀遞石——易卜拉欣立足之石至今留有其足印。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Ibrahim came to his son Ismail, whom he had left with his mother Hagar near the Zamzam well, and asked his wife, 'Where has Ismail gone?' She replied, 'He has gone to hunt for us.' He asked about their living and their condition, and she said, 'We live in misery; we are living in hardship and wretchedness,' and she complained to him. He said, 'When your husband returns, give my salutation to him, and tell him to change the threshold of his gate.' When Ismail came, he seemed to have sensed something, and said, 'Did anyone come to you?' She said, 'Yes, an old man of such and such appearance came and asked me about you, and I told him, and he asked about our livelihood, and I told him that we were in a very hard state.' Ismail said, 'Did he advise you anything?' She said, 'Yes, he commanded me to give you his salutation and said: Change the threshold of your gate.' Ismail said, 'It was my father, and he has commanded me to divorce you. Go back to your family.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3364; not verbatim.

passages.text: Then Ibrahim came again after some years and found a new wife, who treated him well and said they lived in plenty. He told her to give his salutation and to tell her husband to keep the threshold of his gate. Ismail said, 'That was my father, and you are the threshold; he has commanded me to keep you.' Then the two built the House: Ibrahim stood on the stone (Maqam Ibrahim) and Ismail handed him the stones, and Ibrahim laid them until the wall was raised, and they prayed: 'Our Lord, accept this from us.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3365; not verbatim.

title.en: Created From a Rib: Kindness to Women

region.zh: 麥地那朝覲時的教導（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Nikah, no. 5185 (variant: Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 5186); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Nikah, no. 5185 — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day must not hurt his neighbour. And the woman was created from a rib: you will not be able to set her straight in one straight line, but if you take care of her you will benefit; and if you try to straighten her, you will break her, and breaking her is divorcing her. Treat women kindly, for the best of men is he who is best to his wife.
summary.zh: 凡信主與末日者，勿傷其鄰。女子造自肋骨：你無法使其完全正直，若善待之則得益；若強使之直則折之，折之即離婚。善待婦女；男人中之最優者，乃善於待其妻者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; gender imagery is read here as an ethical metaphor within the tradition's own frame.

passages.text: The Prophet said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day should not hurt his neighbour; and he said: Treat women kindly, for woman has been created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is the upper part; if you try to straighten it you will break it, and if you leave it as it is, it will remain crooked; so treat women kindly.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Nikah, no. 5185; not verbatim.

title.en: The Prophet's Swollen Feet in Night Prayer

region.zh: 麥地那阿伊莎的居室（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127 (variant: no. 4837); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127 — narrated by Aisha

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Aisha finds the Prophet praying in the night until his feet become swollen. 'Why do you do this, when God has forgiven you your former and latter sins?' He answers: 'Should I not be a thankful servant?' And once when she thinks of the days and nights of prayer, she is told: 'Your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you — so observe the fast and also break it, and pray and also sleep.'
summary.zh: 阿伊莎見先知夜禮至雙足腫脹。『主已赦你前後之罪，何故如此？』他答：『我豈不當做一感恩的僕人？』又有一夜她想及日夜禮拜之事，被告知：『你的身體對你有權利，你的家屬對你也有權利——當齋戒亦開齋，當禮拜亦睡眠。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: One night the Prophet was engaged in prayer till his feet became swollen. When he was asked, 'Why do you undergo such hardships, although all your past and future sins have been forgiven?' he said: 'Should I not be a thankful servant of God?' And on another occasion he was found praying in the night, and Aisha asked him about his standing so long, and he said: 'I said: Should I not be a grateful servant of God?'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127; not verbatim.

passages.text: The deeds most loved by God are those done regularly, even if they are few. And he said to Aisha: 'Your body has a right over you, and your family has a right over you; so observe the fast and also break the fast, and pray at night and also sleep.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Tahajjud, no. 1127 (closing tradition); not verbatim.

title.en: Hudhayfa's Questioning: Signs of the Last Hour
title.zh: 胡達法的追問：末時之兆

region.zh: 麥地那晚間聚會（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086 (variant: no. 6502); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086 — narrated by Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: People ask Hudhayfa what good he gathered from the Prophet, and he says he was with him among the Companions and asked about evil: 'O Prophet of God, we were in ignorance and evil, and God has brought this good to us; will there be any evil after this good?' He said: 'Yes.' 'And will there be any good after this evil?' 'Yes, but it will be tainted.' 'And will there be any evil after it?' 'Yes, call to prayer will be heard from it, but the callers are not rightly guided; there will be mountains of reeds.'
summary.zh: 眾人問胡達法從先知處得了什麼；他說曾在聖門弟子中，曾問惡事：『主的先知啊，我們本處於愚昧與惡之中，主降此善於我們；此善之後還有惡嗎？』——『有。』『此惡之後還有善嗎？』——『有，但混雜不純。』『其後還有惡嗎？』——『有：其中將聞宣禮聲，而宣禮者不受正導。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; apocalyptic signs kept as spoken in the text.

passages.text: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: People used to ask the Prophet about good, but I used to ask him about evil, fearing lest it overtake me. I said, 'O Prophet of God, we were in ignorance and evil, and God has brought this good to us; will there be any evil after this good?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And will there be any good after this evil?' He said, 'Yes, but it will be tainted.' I said, 'How will it be tainted?' He said, 'There will be people who will lead others according to a path other than my tradition; you will hear of their acts and disapprove of them.' I said, 'And will there be evil after this good?' He said, 'Yes: callers at the gates of Hell; whoever responds to their call will be thrown into the fire.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086; not verbatim.

passages.text: I said, 'O Prophet of God, describe them for us.' He said, 'They are from our people, and they will speak our language.' I said, 'What do you command me to do if that should happen?' He said, 'Adhere to the community of the Muslims and their leader.' I said, 'What if they have neither community nor leader?' He said, 'Keep away from all those sects, even if you have to bite the root of a tree until death comes to you while you are in that state.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7086; not verbatim.

region.en: Abwa, on the road between Mecca and Medina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥加麥地那之間的阿布瓦（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sunan Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Adab, no. 2578; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sunan Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Adab, no. 2578 — narrated by Aisha

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet races with Aisha and she beats him; later, when she has put on weight, she races him again and he wins. 'This is for that' — the earlier victory is repaid. The tale belongs to the Prophet's domestic tenderness, remembered after his death.
summary.zh: 先知與阿伊莎賽跑，她勝了他；日後她體重增加再賽，他勝了她。『這次抵那次』——早先之勝得以償還。此軼事屬先知家庭的溫情，死後猶為人記。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Aisha said: I raced with the Prophet and beat him in the race. Later, when I had put on weight, I raced with him again, and he beat me. He said: 'This is for that previous race of yours.' The Prophet races with Aisha and she beats him; later, when she has put on weight, she races him again and he wins.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sunan Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Adab, no. 2578; not verbatim.
